chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said regarding the Pausing Station: 'Arise from the middle of Urna'. And he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The companions of Arak, there is no Hajj for them'.

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْأَرَاكِ: The companions of Arak, referring to those who stay in that area
key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: The standing (wuquf) at Arafat, a core pillar of Hajj
key_terms.بَطْنِ عُرَنَةَ: The valley of Urna, a specific location near Arafat
key_terms.لَا حَجَّ لَهُمْ: There is no Hajj for them, indicating invalidity or incompleteness

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on standing at Urna and Arak during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the precise boundaries of the obligatory standing (wuquf) at Arafat, distinguishing between the valley of Urna and the area of Arak to ensure ritual validity. It highlights the scholarly emphasis on geographical precision in Hajj rites, where remaining in the latter invalidates the pilgrimage, reflecting the detailed jurisprudential derivations found in Shia fiqh.
